body:
🟠🐛 **Fix · bug: Files dropped while an import runs are silently thrown away**

`run` returns right away when `busy.current` is set (line 64), and nothing tells the user. The header button and the drop zone are disabled while `importing` is true, but `useFileDrop` keeps catching drops on the whole window (`use-file-drop.ts:40-46`). `LibraryPage` sends every drop to `importDropped` (`library-page.tsx:55`), and that calls `run` at line 98. If the user drops a second batch during a long copy (files can be gigabytes), those files are never imported and no toast appears. The `importing` doc at line 27 says "a second one waits for it", which the code doesn't do. Either queue the second call behind the running one (chain it on a stored promise), or show a toast such as "An import is already running" when `busy.current` is set. Then update the comment to match.

🟠📝 **Fix · docs: Doc says every failed file gets its reason, but the multi-failure toast drops the reasons**

The doc says "Every file that failed is named in an error toast with the reason". `failureMessage` in `use-import-videos.ts:109-121` gives a reason only when exactly one file failed. When two or more fail, it uses `importFailedMany` ("Couldn’t import {count} files: {fileNames}"), which lists the names and no reasons. The test at `use-import-videos.test.tsx:95` asserts exactly that. Change the sentence to say that a single failure shows its reason and several failures list only the file names. The other option is to add the reasons to the many-files toast.

🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: "Only videos can be imported" also names video files that were skipped only because they have no path on disk**

`importDropped` (`use-import-videos.ts:86-93`) puts a file in `skipped` for either of two reasons: its extension isn't importable, or `pathForFile` returns "" (for example, a file dragged out of a web page). Both cases get the same message. So a dropped `web.mp4` produces "Only videos can be imported (MP4, MOV, M4V or WebM). Skipped: notes.pdf, web.mp4", which tells the user their MP4 isn't a video. The test at `use-import-videos.test.tsx:137` locks this wording in. Consider a separate message for path-less files, such as "isn’t a file on your computer", or a more neutral wording for the shared one. The same applies to `es.json:624`.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Cristian Sotomayor**

Fixed in [`d1d24c29`](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/commit/d1d24c29d39690c46bd5a6d2a38f57beb5136fd0) on #471 (top of the stack): a drop during a running import now waits for it instead of being discarded (queued in `useImportVideos.run`, with a test).

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Cristian Sotomayor**

Fixed in [`450c9100`](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/commit/450c910079c5692c55a314de82f77fc798135608) on #471 (top of the stack): the doc now says one failed file gets its reason and several failures list the names only.

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Cristian Sotomayor**

Fixed in [`d1d24c29`](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/commit/d1d24c29d39690c46bd5a6d2a38f57beb5136fd0) on #471 (top of the stack): videos with no path on disk get their own toast (`library.importDropNoPath`: "not a file on your computer. Save it first, then drop it again."), separate from "Only videos can be imported".
